verdictReasoning: Corrected after direct DB verification (not the script's blanket if-errorSurfaced branch, which mis-labeled this ERROR-SWALLOWED on first pass): a real, human-visible agent_runs row DOES exist for this run (id 93dbf01b-4d3a-4b5d-a794-f613e20d2ad6, status='failed', error_message='Agent timed out after 60s.', confirmed via direct psql read) -- so the failure is NOT swallowed by the app in the taxonomy's strict sense (a human looking at agent_runs would see it). The real cause, confirmed via StealthEngine's own console output captured in this run: EA-01 tries 3 candidate paths (/giving, /csr, /community) sequentially, each with 3 retry attempts, against the seeded website (a *.example domain that -- like any dead/moved real-world website -- fails DNS resolution); that retry loop alone exceeded BaseAgent's hard 60s per-run ceiling (base-agent.ts AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS) before even reaching Claude or a single successful write. Compare directly to AG-21 (EA-08, sibling agent, same corporate-enrichment-shared.ts helper, same run against the same class of *.example seed domain) which completed in well under 60s and produced a real WORKS write -- the only material difference is EA-08 tries 2 candidate paths vs EA-01's 3, meaning EA-01's fixed per-candidate retry cost (3 paths x 3 attempts) is close enough to the 60s ceiling that any unreachable/slow-to-fail website reliably times the whole run out before it can write anything, including the documented graceful 'no pages found' branch. This is a genuine, generalizable robustness defect (not a harness artifact, not specific to the fake seed domain) distinct from ERROR-SWALLOWED: the agent cannot complete AT ALL against a realistic dead/unreachable-website input, even though the failure is at least recorded to agent_runs. Zero corporate_prospects.enrichment write resulted either way.
